question: How can the existing book reference support the authorized workflow without competing acceptance state?
intended_experience: Support the designer in choosing and testing the intended player experience while keeping routine implementation lightweight. This is a tooling decision, not a new game requirement.

reference.role: Chapter16: decision effort proportional to consequence
Ch11 qualification: established designs can justify detailed planning

applicability: The catalog explicitly includes book-to-runbook integration. Human observation, QA and source retrieval answer different questions.
choice: Reuse the existing pilot catalog and helper for consultation integrity; route current steps through one conductor and acceptance through one runner, as authorized on 2026-10-19.
tradeoff: Small local cooperative controls are inspectable and need no service; they cannot authenticate a same-user human or reviewer.
hypothesis: Source-linked records and one acceptance owner can preserve source qualifications while rejecting stale or insufficient evidence.
challenge_observation: A missing or altered source reference, stale result, omitted required test or absent human decision is accepted, or normal valid completion cannot proceed.
method: Validate the untouched pilot; use disposable positive and deliberate-failure fixtures; obtain a fresh independent requirements-and-evidence audit of the saved tooling candidate.
prototype_limits: No game, renderer, live Unreal bridge, real player or adversarial identity boundary is commissioned by these fixtures.
qualifications: The author supports adaptive knowledge creation and proportionate decision effort; the conductor, schemas, hooks and ledger are our adaptations. Existing mandatory duties stay binding. Established designs may justify detailed planning (printed p. 288); automated QA does not prove enjoyment.
